title: Standby Priming & Activation Coordinator: multi-region readiness orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a centralized Coordinator service and workflows that prime warm standby fleets across regions and assert multi-dimensional readiness before traffic failover. Focus is on: (1) asset priming (model binary, quantized kernels), (2) KV/prefix cache seeding for common workloads, (3) lightweight shadow-canary traffic and probe gating, and (4) cost-conscious activation policies tied to customer tier and SLOs. This ticket scopes the orchestration logic, readiness checks, API contract for Console, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can trigger priming in a target region and report per-node readiness states within 60s of start

Readiness checks include: model load success, kernel compatibility check, GPU memory residency confirmation, KV cache seeding hit-rate >= 15% on synthetic workload, and probe latency percentiles within SLO
Coordinator exposes APIs for: initiate_priming, status_stream, cancel_priming, promote_standby; API contract documented in Confluence and Swagger
Console shows per-customer standby health, expected activation cost estimate, and an override for emergency promote
Automated canary shadowing successfully routes 0.1% production traffic to standby for 10 minutes and validates output parity metrics
Playbook and runbook added to infra Runbooks; post-mortem hooks integrated with incident response
design_notes: Coordinator runs as a control-plane microservice, stateless; uses durable job queue (existing runtime-queue) to track priming steps

Priming steps are staged: (A) allocate nodes w/ placement constraints, (B) load model variant (with quantized fallback), (C) warm KV with sampled prefixes from observed top-k prompts, (D) run shadow canary traffic + functional tests, (E) assert readiness and mark promotable
Use feature flags to gate aggressive priming (per-customer deployment). Default policy: warm 2 nodes per zone for P0 customers, 1 node per zone for P1, deferred for P2/P3
Fallback model variant mapping table maintained in config store: e.g., fp16->int8-quantized variant compatibility must be validated at priming time
Cost trade-off: warm nodes increase base monthly cost; we'll compute projected cost per hour and expose to Console. Consider idle-time auto-suspend with fast resume for long-tail windows
Concurrency concerns: priming is IO and memory heavy; limit concurrent priming per-region to avoid contention with serving lanes
implementation_steps: 1) API: define REST endpoints and event shapes; add Swagger spec to /confluence/display/RW/Standby+Coordinator
2) Control-plane: implement Coordinator service using existing infra SDK; job orchestration uses runtime-queue with idempotent steps
3) Priming worker: extend runtime agent to support dry-load and kv-seed endpoints and return readiness fingerprints
4) Shadowing harness: reuse traffic-duplication pipeline; add lightweight comparator to compute semantic divergence and latency delta
5) Console integration: new standby dashboard, cost estimate widget, manual promote button (feature-flagged)
6) Access control: ensure promote endpoints honor RBAC and audit-logging
7) Tests: unit + e2e in staging with synthetic workload and intentional kernel incompatibilities
testing_plan: Staging test: simulate region failure and validate Coordinator promotes standby and application latency remains under SLO
Chaos test: introduce kernel mismatch on one node to verify Prime step fails fast and fallback variant loads
KV-seed verification: generate synthetic prefix traffic to validate seeding meets hit-rate threshold within 5 minutes
Shadow parity test: assert semantic divergence < threshold for 95% sample; flag customers when exceeded
Load test: ensure concurrent priming (n=5) in a region does not degrade active serving p95 by >10%
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood on non-critical tenants; monitor costs and flakiness (2 weeks)
Phase 1: opt-in for P0 customers behind feature flag; enable manual promote; collect metrics (4 weeks)
Phase 2: automated policy for P0 with soft failover (shadow then promote) and cost alerts (6 weeks)
Phase 3: full rollout to Dedicated customers with SLA-linked activation (after 90-day stability)
Rollback: cancel_priming + drain promoted nodes; revert traffic routing to origin region
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: priming_duration_seconds (histogram) per region, per model_variant
Alert: priming_duration > 10m for 5% of jobs => PagerDuty (oncall-runtime)
Metric: kv_seed_hit_rate (gauge) measured during priming; alert if < configured threshold
Metric: shadow_divergence_rate; fire high-severity if > 5% for 10m
